column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:net module
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Loadable module of HTTP / API access words that were moved out of the
# core registry. They are reached only after `import`, under the `Net`
# namespace: `import "aql:net" Net.word args`.
#   Net.fetch    — perform an HTTP request
#   Net.prepare  — build a request from an API descriptor (no send)
#   Net.direct   — build-and-send a request against an API descriptor
# fetch/prepare/direct need a live network or an API SDK to exercise
# end-to-end (covered by the Go fetch / prepare_direct tests), so the
# spec here pins the namespace binding and the move out of core.
# §1  import binds the Net namespace (the module's exported namespace name)
import "aql:net" convert List Net.$module
column3: import binds the Net namespace

column1: # §2  negative — the words are gone from core (unbound without import)
fetch "http://x"
column3: `fetch` is no longer a core word

column1: Net.fetch "http://x"
column3: `Net` is unbound without `import`

column1: # §3  prepare / direct — building a request from an API descriptor. A full
#     send needs a live network / API SDK (covered by the Go fetch /
#     prepare_direct tests), but the descriptor-validation path is reachable
#     and deterministic: an "api"-kind descriptor missing its "spec" is
#     rejected, exercising dispatch through the Net.prepare / Net.direct
#     wrappers without any network.
import "aql:net" Net.prepare {kind:"api"}
column3: prepare validates the API descriptor

column1: import "aql:net" Net.direct {kind:"api"}
column3: direct validates the API descriptor

column1: # module-owned Fetch types — per-import mints, exported literals
# (former global FixedIDs 3000-3002 retired; a fetch Response value
# carries the module-minted Net.Response type).
import "aql:net"  Net.Response is Net.Fetch
column3: Response is a lattice child of the module's Fetch root

column1: import "aql:net"  Net.Request is Net.Fetch
column3: Request is a lattice child of the module's Fetch root

column1: import "aql:net"  typeof Net.Response
column3: the exported literal IS its lattice node (typeof reports the parent)

column1: # §4  Tier-1 sockets — Listener/Socket handles, bind/dial, passive reads.
#     Every row binds an ephemeral port ({tcp: 0}) and reads it back via
#     Net.addr so outputs stay deterministic.
# listen / addr / close: bind, inspect the bound port, release
import "aql:net" def l (Net.listen {tcp: 0}) def a (Net.addr l) Net.close l; a.port gt 0
column3: Net.listen binds; Net.addr reports the ephemeral port; Net.close releases

column1: # the exported handle types (module type literals)
import "aql:net" canon Net.Socket
column3: Net.Socket is the connection-handle type literal

column1: import "aql:net" canon Net.Listener
column3: Net.Listener is the listen-socket type literal

column1: # listener identity: a bound listener IS a Net.Listener
import "aql:net" def l (Net.listen {tcp: 0}) def ok (l is Net.Listener) Net.close l; ok
column3: a bound listener is a Net.Listener

column1: # accept: dial from this thread first — the kernel backlog holds the pending
# connection, so the subsequent accept is deterministic (no spawn race); the
# {within} deadline is belt-and-braces so the row can never hang the runner

import "aql:net" def l (Net.listen {tcp: 0}) def a (Net.addr l) def s (Net.connect-raw {tcp: (join "" ["127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])}) def c (Net.accept l {within: 5000}) Net.send-bytes (convert Bytes "x") s; def g (convert String (Net.recv-bytes c 1 {within: 5000})) Net.close s; Net.close c; Net.close l; g
column3: Net.accept yields the pending connection and Net.recv-bytes reads exactly n

column1: # negative — accept honours {within}: an idle listener raises `timeout`
import "aql:net" def l (Net.listen {tcp: 0}) def code (do [ Net.accept l {within: 60} ] error [ dot code ]) Net.close l; code eq timeout/q
column3: Net.accept with {within: ms} times out instead of blocking forever

column1: # serve-raw echo over connect-raw: recv-until frames a line, send-bytes replies

import "aql:net" def l (Net.serve-raw {tcp: 0} ([c:Any] => [ Net.send-bytes (Net.recv-until c (convert Bytes "\n") {within: 5000}) c ])) def a (Net.addr l) def s (Net.connect-raw {tcp: (join "" ["127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])}) Net.send-bytes (convert Bytes "ping\n") s; def r (convert String (Net.recv-bytes s 4 {within: 5000})) Net.close s; Net.close l; r
column3: serve-raw accept-loop + connect-raw dial + recv-until framing round-trip

column1: # peer / shutdown / recv deadline: a silent peer raises `timeout`

import "aql:net" def l (Net.listen {tcp: 0}) def a (Net.addr l) def s (Net.connect-raw {tcp: (join "" ["127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])}) def p (Net.peer s) Net.shutdown s "write"; def code (do [ Net.recv s 1 {within: 60} ] error [ dot code ]) Net.close s; Net.close l; (p.port gt 0) and (code eq timeout/q)
column3: Net.peer reports the remote; Net.shutdown half-closes; Net.recv honours {within}

column1: # negative — malformed options are refused loudly
import "aql:net" Net.listen {}
column3: listen needs a tcp: (or unix:) option

column1: import "aql:net" Net.listen {tcp: -1}
column3: listen rejects an out-of-range port

column1: import "aql:net" Net.connect-raw {tcp: 99}
column3: connect-raw wants a "host:port" String

column1: # §5  Tier-2 codecs — a codec is a {decode encode} map; built-ins are values.
import "aql:net" Net.lines get "name"
column3: Net.lines is the newline-delimited text codec value

column1: import "aql:net" Net.json-lines get "name"
column3: Net.json-lines is the NDJSON codec value

column1: import "aql:net" Net.http get "name"
column3: Net.http is the HTTP/1.1 codec value

column1: # listen {codec} service + connect → Endpoint: a lines echo round-trip

import "aql:net" def svc (service {}) add {} ([r:Map state:Any] => [ r.line ]) svc def l (Net.listen {tcp: 0 codec: Net.lines} svc) def a (Net.addr l) def e (Net.connect {tcp: (join "" ["127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)]) codec: Net.lines}) def r (call {line: "ok"} e {timeout: 5000}) Net.close e; Net.close l; r.line
column3: listen exposes a service over a codec; connect returns a callable Endpoint

column1: # negative — a wire protocol is never implicit
import "aql:net" def svc (service {}) Net.listen {tcp: 0} svc
column3: listen over a service requires an explicit codec

column1: import "aql:net" Net.connect {tcp: "127.0.0.1:1"}
column3: connect requires an explicit codec

column1: # --- Fetch accessor word extensions: import transplants these onto the
# importer's bare dot/get/dotr/getr/has so a Response reads directly.
# Behaviour rows use the bare spelling (what guests write); the
# qualified rows pin the exports themselves (ADR-003) and that the
# overloads stay anchored on Fetch rather than leaking to other types.

import "aql:net" def l (Net.serve-raw {tcp: 0} ([c:Any] => [ Net.recv-until c (convert Bytes "

") {within: 5000}; Net.send-bytes (convert Bytes "HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Content-Length: 0

") c ])) def a (Net.addr l) def r (Net.fetch (join "" ["http://127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])) def v (r.status) Net.close l; v
column3: a Response answers .field directly — no convert Map step

import "aql:net" def l (Net.serve-raw {tcp: 0} ([c:Any] => [ Net.recv-until c (convert Bytes "

") {within: 5000}; Net.send-bytes (convert Bytes "HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Content-Length: 0

") c ])) def a (Net.addr l) def r (Net.fetch (join "" ["http://127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])) def v (r.nope) Net.close l; v
column3: a missing Response field reads none (lenient, like a Map)

column1:
import "aql:net" def l (Net.serve-raw {tcp: 0} ([c:Any] => [ Net.recv-until c (convert Bytes "

") {within: 5000}; Net.send-bytes (convert Bytes "HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Content-Length: 0

") c ])) def a (Net.addr l) def r (Net.fetch (join "" ["http://127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])) def v (do [r!.nope] error [dot code]) Net.close l; v
column3: the strict twin raises where the lenient read returns none

import "aql:net" def l (Net.serve-raw {tcp: 0} ([c:Any] => [ Net.recv-until c (convert Bytes "

") {within: 5000}; Net.send-bytes (convert Bytes "HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Content-Length: 0

") c ])) def a (Net.addr l) def r (Net.fetch (join "" ["http://127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])) def v (r has "status") Net.close l; v

import "aql:net" def l (Net.serve-raw {tcp: 0} ([c:Any] => [ Net.recv-until c (convert Bytes "

") {within: 5000}; Net.send-bytes (convert Bytes "HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Content-Length: 0

") c ])) def a (Net.addr l) def r (Net.fetch (join "" ["http://127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])) def v (convert Map r) Net.close l; v.status

column3: Net.dot is exported as a Fetch-only accessor overload

column3: Net.get likewise

column1: # --- Server-side TLS (design/NETWORK-TLS-PLAN.0.md §5 phase 6). A
# listener PRESENTS a credential and may DEMAND one back; a dial
# verifies one and may present one. Each side rejects the other's keys
# by name — a `verify: false` quietly accepted on a listener would read
# as configured while configuring nothing. The positive round trip needs
# a host-registered credential, which AQL source cannot create by
# design, so it lives in net_socket_tlsserver_test.go.
import "aql:net" Net.listen {tcp: 0  tls: {}}
column3: a TLS server with no certificate has nothing to present

column1: import "aql:net" Net.listen {tcp: 0  tls: {identity: nobody/q}}
column3: guest source names a credential; only the host registers one

column1: import "aql:net" Net.listen {tcp: 0  tls: {identity: srv/q  verify: false}}
column3: verify: is a dial option — a server verifies no server chain

column1: import "aql:net" Net.listen {tcp: 0  tls: {identity: srv/q  ca: "x"}}
column3: a server names its client roots with require-client:

column1: import "aql:net" Net.listen {tcp: 0  tls: {identity: srv/q  sni: "x"}}
column3: sni: is what a client sends, not what a server reads

column1: import "aql:net" Net.listen {tcp: 0  tls: {identity: srv/q  nope: 1}}
column3: an unknown listen tls: key is refused, never ignored

column1: import "aql:net" Net.connect-raw {tcp: "127.0.0.1:1"  tls: {require-client: "x"}}
column3: require-client: is a listen option

column1: import "aql:net" def l (Net.serve-raw {tcp: 0} ([c:Any] => [ Net.recv c 1 {within: 5000} ])) def a (Net.addr l) def s (Net.connect-raw {tcp: (join "" ["127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])}) def v (Net.peer-cert s) Net.close s; Net.close l; v
column3: peer-cert on a plain socket is None — no TLS means no proven peer
